reason: Two of the four concrete sub-requirements the issue names are demonstrably unmet: the intake.md write-failure path still returns 0 with outcome=pass (SPEC-4), and six pre-existing `| atomic_write` calls outside the two bug-fix files lack `|| true`, causing the full-codebase lint to fail (SPEC-8); additionally, new comment text at `plugin.sh:1209` introduces a lint-disposition-words violation that breaks `npm run lint`.

unmet: R-1 (intake.md, SPEC-4): The test at `plugins/agent/intake/tests/intake-result-test.sh` fails with "expected: 1, got: 0" and "expected: broken, got: pass". Although the code in `plugins/agent/intake/plugin.sh` does capture `PIPESTATUS[1]` after the `intake.md` write and checks `_im_aw_rc != 0`, the test run shows `_intake_run_inner` returns 0 and the result remains "pass" when that write fails — the fix is present in the diff but does not work in practice for this path.

R-1 (R3/SPEC-8): The test at `tests/unit/plugin-primary-output-atomic-test.sh` fails with "missing || true at: core/state/resume.sh:80 core/output/stage-io.sh:637 plugins/agent/build/lib/secrets.sh:172 plugins/tool/test/lib/own-checks.sh:72,96,101". None of these six files appear in the diff — they were not changed — so the pre-existing unchecked calls were not annotated. SPEC-8 requires all 13 pre-existing calls to carry `|| true`; six do not, and `npm run lint` (via the newly wired `lint-atomic-write-unchecked.sh`) would therefore fail on the real codebase.

R-1 (lint, disposition-words regression): `npm run lint` fails with `lint-disposition-words: tool/test/plugin.sh:1209 writes outcome 'is'`. The new multi-line comment block added to the fallback path in `plugins/tool/test/plugin.sh` (the line `# no second stage_result_add call is needed.`) is parsed by `lint-disposition-words` as a `stage_result_add` invocation with disposition word `is`. This is a regression introduced by the diff that blocks lint from passing.
unsure: R-1 (SPEC-1/SPEC-2, test-first validity): The acceptance-check stage reported that SPEC-1 and SPEC-2's tests "already pass on the code from before this change," meaning the tests may not catch reversion of the fix. The REQUIREMENTS stage claims the opposite ("its test failed on the old code and passes now"), and my reading of the old code logic supports the REQUIREMENTS assessment, but the before-test check timed out so neither stage can be fully trusted. I cannot determine with certainty whether SPEC-1/SPEC-2's tests are falsifiable against the old code.
